items.evidence: "Agnes presented the wooden, customizable remote" - Agnes is the User Interface Designer who gave the presentation.
"A flip-panel LCD is included provisionally" and "The back and flip case could have customized designs."

Notes give the component list and "€9.95 against a €12.50 budget; adding the LCD could add €2–€3" but do not say the Project Manager presented it. The transcript does not support the key's claim that the budget ruled out the LCD (Marketing Expert said adding it brings the cost to about 12-12.5, and the Industrial Designer said 'we can put the LCD in'); the notes match the transcript here.

"the company representative will pursue lower costs" and action item to negotiate with vendors (owner: "Speaker 1"). Owner not clearly named as the Project Manager. In the transcript the savings were meant for marketing and promotion, not specifically the display.

"Selling two million units in year one would require 25% of the market"; "the LCD and the company's sales and profit goals put feasibility in doubt"; "The group questioned whether the company could reach its two-million-unit and €50 million profit targets."
"Christine proposed online ordering and direct shipment as an alternative sales channel"; Amazon/eBay and customization images mentioned.

"Agnes said the project had no redesign time if users found problems" and "The company representative chose to keep the basic design for market introduction and use customer feedback for a second generation."
"coordinating a user-tested launch with a major sports event" and "a campaign with Sony Pictures around a DVD release."
"Negotiate lower production costs with vendors and discuss cost reductions with management (owner: Speaker 1)" - task is right but owner is given only as "Speaker 1", not the Project Manager.
"Try to convince management to pursue a campaign with Sony Pictures (owner: Speaker 1)" - covers the DVD campaign only, not the sports-event launch idea, and owner is "Speaker 1".
Nothing about the Project Manager leaving it to Ed (Marketing Expert) to take over once production is done.

Notes say "Production evaluation was expected in two to four weeks" but do not say evaluation follows production of real units; the transcript itself is muddled ('wait for the production, then you can evaluate' vs 'prototype product evaluation' in two weeks).

LCD "included provisionally" and "The group considered the side as an accessible placement", but notes call microphone location "unresolved" even though the Project Manager and others agreed the side was a good idea.
Negotiation to cut production cost is noted, but not tied to the Project Manager by role and not linked to fitting the display (transcript links it to marketing money).

Sports-event launch and Sony Pictures DVD campaign, with "The company representative said they would try to convince management." Matches the transcript, where these were proposals the Project Manager agreed to push.
"The company representative chose to keep the basic design for market introduction and use customer feedback for a second generation."

Notes describe a production evaluation in 2-4 weeks and Christine proposing testing prototypes, but do not state that evaluation will happen after real units are produced rather than on the prototype.

Notes cover the profit-goal doubt ("put feasibility in doubt", 25% of market, €25 profit per unit) but not that budget plans must change. Transcript shows the components incl. LCD roughly fit the 12.5 budget, so the key overstates the budget part.
"wanted to proceed with the current design, while the others argued for user testing and enough time to respond"; "Agnes said the project had no redesign time."

errors.claim: Christine estimated the case could cost €1 for material and labor.
errors.why_wrong: The €1 case figure came from the Project Manager's cost sheet; Christine (Industrial Designer) only reacted to it with surprise.

errors.claim: Prototypes would be made outside the company's factory.
errors.why_wrong: The transcript says the product evaluation/testing would not be done in the factory, not that prototypes would be made elsewhere.
After discussion the group, including the Project Manager ('the sides maybe is good. That's good idea'), agreed the side was the place for the microphone.
